## Claims
- [source-backed] Equation **(8)** is
  \[
  \left\{
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}
  \sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}}
  c_{(i^j,\lambda),\theta}^{\nu}A_{\lambda,\theta}
  =\chi(\nu)\ \middle|\ \nu\in\decomp_{\varphi}
  \right\},
  \qquad
  \chi(\nu)=
  \begin{cases}
  f_{\nu_B}&\text{if \(\nu\) is tall},\\
  0&\text{if \(\nu\) is wide}.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 332-340]
- [source-backed] Equation **(9)** is
  \[
  \mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_\lambda\otimes\overline{s}_\mu)=
  \begin{cases}
  \overline{\Delta(s_\lambda)}-(\overline{s}_\lambda\otimes1)
  &\text{if \(\overline{s}_\mu=1\)},\\
  \overline{\Delta(s_\lambda)}(1\otimes\overline{s}_\mu)
  &\text{if \(\overline{s}_\mu\neq1\)}.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 387-397]
- [source-backed] Equation **(10)** is
  \[
  \xi^{(m)}=\xi^{(m-1)}
  -\gamma\mathrm{CP}\!\left(
  \overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes
  (\overline{s}_{\mu^{(1)}}\cdots\overline{s}_{\mu^{(k)}})
  \right).
  \]
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 625-632]
- [source-backed] **Theorem 4.4.** For any valid
  \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), the equations
  \[
  \left\{\linear_{\varphi}(\nu)=d_{\nu}\mid
  \nu\in\decomp_{\varphi}\right\}
  \]
  are inconsistent whenever \(d_\nu=0\) for all wide \(\nu\), and
  \(d_\rho\neq0\) for some tall \(\rho\). Its proof first uses
  \(N\leq\min(j,n-r-i)\) and Lemma 4.2, then enlarges to
  \(\widehat n=4^qn,\widehat r=2^qr,\widehat j=2^qj\) when necessary and applies Lemma 4.3. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-818]
- [source-backed] **Theorem 4.5.** For any valid
  \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), there is no syzygy
  \[
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|=N}}
  \overline{s}_{(i^j,\lambda)}f_\lambda
  =
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}
  f_\lambda\overline{s}_{(i^j,\lambda)}
  \]
  with nonzero left-hand side. The proof invokes Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-826]
